population.label: Caucasian (European background; used for Australian patients of European background)

extractedBy: Task 6 AI reader A and AI reader B (mcnamara1984.a/.b, Tables III and VI rows)
curation.notes: Ruling P23: one set per McNamara sample. Ruling P24: mcnamara1984-caucasian.a.json not used (not independent); the Table III and VI rows of mcnamara1984-caucasian.b.json were compared row by row against the independent Task 6 extractions mcnamara1984.a.json and .b.json, which hold the same rows (script comparison 2026-10-08, positive control: two planted changes found): 72 rows compared with each, 0 differences. Table III also re-read on the page image (PDF p. 5 = p. 453) because its text layer is garbled (it reads 91.1 for the girls' 6-year Co-Gn, the page 97.7): every value agrees with the three readings. Girls' 6-year differential SD 8.1 kept as printed, noted (merge notes). Selection class-I-balanced (owner ruling MCN-1, 8 Oct, fix round 1; was unknown): p. 462 gives the Bolton standards (Table VI) as an example of well-balanced faces; p. 450 describes them as the Bolton standards children, retraced longitudinally by Behrents and McNamara. With it, Bolton ranks before Burlington (selection unknown) where both cover a child's age (rule 5), no longer by file order. Single printed ages entered as [a, a]; n 16 per sex per age (table headings). Scale enlarged 8% (p. 451; headings 'standardized 8% enlargement'). Incisor distances close (facial surface, M1).

caveats: 'Caucasian' is our label: the paper never states the samples' ethnicity (it says nothing about ancestry).

The children of the Bolton standards (Bolton-Brush study, Cleveland), whose longitudinal records were retraced (p. 450): 16 per sex at each age (Tables III and VI). The paper gives no whole-sample count. It calls them well-balanced faces (p. 462 gives the Bolton standards as an example of well-balanced faces), so the set is class-I balanced (owner ruling MCN-1, 8 Oct); no other selection criteria are given.

8% film enlargement: p. 451 says the measures from all these samples include an 8% enlargement wherever possible; the table heading says 'standardized 8% enlargement'. The app shows mm values at true size (÷ 1.08) with the printed value.
Values are printed at single ages (6, 9, 12, 14, 16, 18 y). A child between two printed ages gets the nearest printed age, marked as not his age (no interpolation is used for this set).
Girls' 6-year maxillomandibular differential: SD 8.1 as printed — possibly a misprint (every other differential SD is 2.2-4.1).
Not in the catalogue: Table VII annual increments (p. 465).
